summary: Nicolas Revire works in Buddhist studies and archaeology. He studied at Silpakorn University (2012-2013) and with Claudine Bautze-Picron, Peter Skilling, and Michel Jacq-Hergoualc'h, later holding a post at Thammasat University (attested 2016).
Nicolas Sihlé is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He served as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Anthropology at the University of Virginia (attested 2010).

Linguist and Tibetologist Nicolas Tournadre earned his PhD at Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Claude Hagège (~1986-1992). He held posts at INALCO (~1992-1995), Paris 8 (~1995-2004), University of Provence (~2004-2011), and Aix-Marseille University (~2012).
Active in Buddhist and religious studies, Nicole Baden studied under traditional teacher Richard Baker, whom she succeeded in 2024.

Nicole Vandier-Nicolas specialized in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and art history. She taught Chinese art at the École du Louvre and served on the faculty of École nationale des langues orientales vivantes/INALCO (~1958-1977).

Niels Ludvig Westergaard was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Copenhagen, Bonn (under Christian Lassen), Paris, and Oxford. He spent his career at the University of Copenhagen, becoming professor of Indian and Oriental philology (1850) and Rektor (1867-1868).
Nigel Allan worked as Curator of Oriental Books and Manuscripts at the Wellcome Institute for the History of Medicine (attested 1993), where he succeeded Marianne Winder.

Niharranjan Ray studied at Calcutta and Leiden universities. He served at the University of Calcutta as Chief Librarian (1936) and Bageswari Professor of Fine Arts (1946-1965), and later as Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (1965-1970).
Nika Jovic is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her Magistra der Philosophie at the University of Vienna (attested 2010) under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Nikolai Solmsdorf, a Tibetologist, completed his PhD at the University of Munich under Franz-Karl Ehrhard (attested 2013). He was affiliated with the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2013).
Linguist Nikolai Trubetzkoy studied at Moscow University and under August Leskien. He taught at Sofia University (~1920-1922) before holding a post at the University of Vienna (~1922-1938).

Historian Nile Green held a post at the University of Manchester (~2005-2007) and has served as Professor and Ibn Khaldun Endowed Chair in World History at the University of California, Los Angeles since ~2007.

Nina Mirnig is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She has held posts at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2020) and the University of Vienna (attested 2026).

Ninian Smart studied at Oxford. In religious studies and philosophy, he held professorships at Birmingham (1961), Lancaster University (1967-1982), and the University of California, Santa Barbara (1976-1998).
Nira Wickramasinghe studied at the University of Paris and the University of Oxford. She became Professor of Modern South Asian Studies at Leiden University around 2010.

Indologist Nirajan Kafle earned his doctorate at Leiden University under Peter C. Bisschop (-2015). He held posts at the University of Naples 'L'Orientale' (attested 2019) and Leiden University (attested 2021).

Niranjan Prasad Chakravarti studied at Paris, Berlin, and Cambridge (PhD ~1926). He served the Archaeological Survey of India in various capacities, ultimately becoming Director General of Archaeology in India (1948-1950).

Niras Ruangsan, a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology, earned a PhD at the University of Sydney (attested 2015) under the supervision of Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle, Peter Oldmeadow, Mark Allon, and Prayong Seanburan.

Nirbhay N. Singh has held posts as Professor at Virginia Commonwealth University, Director of the Commonwealth Institute for Family Studies, and Clinical Professor of Psychiatry and Health Behavior at Augusta University (attested 2015-2018).

Tibetologist and historian Nirmal Chandra Sinha studied at Presidency University and Calcutta University. He worked at the National Archives of India (~1942-1958) and served as founder director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (1958-1987).
